analyst_view.overall: Early view: a winner-take-all Wild Card at Lumen Field, with the winner facing top seed Vancouver; a draw after 90 minutes goes straight to penalties. Seattle squeezed in with a 2-1 win over LAFC despite being outshot 24-5, and are without Pedro de la Vega, Yeimar Gomez Andrade and Nikola Petkovic, with Jordan Morris worth watching after he went off after 24 minutes on Decision Day. Real Salt Lake went 5-2-1 down the stretch and have Sergi Solans (15 goals); the site lists JuanMa Sanabria as banned after his Decision Day yellow, which I could not confirm in club or league reports.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean a little lower: Pablo Mastroeni set Real Salt Lake up in a 5-4-1 on Decision Day, Seattle's attack is thinner without de la Vega and possibly Morris, and the last playoff meeting between these two, in 2021, finished 0-0. RSL have scored in eight straight league games, so a 1-1 or 2-0 fits better than a shootout.

corners.text: The site expects 11.1 corners, with 6.4 for Seattle. I lean lower: Seattle won just two corners against LAFC and played on the break, and with de la Vega out and Morris a doubt they have fewer wide runners to win them. RSL took six against the Galaxy, so I see something nearer nine than eleven.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards and lean under 4.5. I lean higher: RSL were booked four times in their must-win game against the Galaxy (Henry, Sanabria, de Fougerolles, Solans) and Seattle collected three late yellows protecting their lead over LAFC. A knockout game between old playoff rivals should carry at least that much edge.

shots.text: The site expects 29.3 shots, roughly even. I lean lower because neither side has been a high-volume team lately: Seattle had five shots against LAFC and relied on Andrew Thomas's saves, and RSL's back five is built to limit chances. RSL did take 20 shots against a Galaxy side chasing the game, so this depends on who scores first.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. I lean slightly lower in line with fewer shots overall: Seattle put three on target on Decision Day, and a cautious RSL away from home is unlikely to repeat the nine they managed against the Galaxy in Utah.
